title: DVWA security.php level change: CSRF token enforced (candidate not vulnerable)
request_sequence: [security=low] GET http://dvwa/security.php (dvwa_admin) -> token d0231961db26307f8550500dcc16fc28, level low

POST http://dvwa/security.php security=low&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] (restore) -> 302; GET shows 'Security level set to low', level low
response_evidence: [security=low] The security-level form enforces a per-page user_token. A POST without user_token was rejected: the follow-up page displays 'CSRF token is incorrect' and the level remained 'low'. The same POST with the valid token from the rendered form succeeded: the page displayed 'Security level set to high'. The level was then restored to low with a fresh token. Because the state-changing request is gated by a valid, page-bound anti-CSRF token, a cross-site forged POST without the token is ignored, so the CWE-352 candidate is not exploitable as CSRF. Verdict: rejected (anti-CSRF token is enforced). Note: the token check is a valid defense; the observed behavior does not support the suspected CWE.
